history.period: Modern/recent construction (grand new temple in final construction stage)
history.summary: A Hindu Khatu Shyam Ji temple on Yamuna Kinara Road, Jeoni Mandi, Civil Lines, Agra (282004) — the most prominent of several Khatu Shyam shrines in Agra (others include the Agra-Jalesar Road/Nai Ki Sarai temple and the Nehru Market/Belanganj shrine, whose listing coordinates nearly coincide with this one — identity ambiguity flagged). Khatu Shyam Baba is venerated as Barbarika, the grandson of Bhima, embodying the ideal of charity and devotion ('Haare ka Sahara'). Local listing descriptions report a grand new temple built in Rajasthani architectural style with the deity to be seated on a 100-kg silver throne; craftsmen of Vrindavan's Prem Mandir are reported to be giving the three sections their distinctive look. This temple is distinct from the famous Khatu Shyamji temple at Khatu, Sikar, Rajasthan (CSV seq 2177 — different temple, different state) and from Mahesh's other Khatu Shyam records.

name: Shri Khatu Shyam Ji Temple, Agra
town_description: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna in western Uttar Pradesh, was the capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, and is home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Civil Lines is the colonial-era cantonment and administrative quarter north of the old city, containing the Jeoni Mandi area on Mahatma Gandhi Road near the Yamuna.

travel.railway: Yamuna Bridge railway station is about 0.92 km away (per yappe); Agra Cantt and Agra Fort are the main stations.
travel.road: On Yamuna Kinara Road / Mahatma Gandhi Road, Jeoni Mandi, Civil Lines, Agra; parking reported as limited.
